LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we repeat some sounds, words and lines in a poem?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem
2. describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem
3. appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem

What this means
In this part you learn to identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems to a partner. (skill: describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem.
3. Practise this skill: describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of repetition and rhyme in a poem.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we repeat some sounds, words and lines in a poem?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem.
5. Be able to: describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
